rules.cwe_name: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Files
rules.description: Sensitive information is written to debug or diagnostic log files.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: The 'eval' function and the 'Function' constructor execute strings as code. This is dangerous and impedes program analysis and understanding. Consequently, these two functions should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Directly sending file data in an outbound network request can indicate unauthorized information disclosure.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Logging sensitive information without encryption or hashing can expose it to an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
rules.description: Propagating stack trace information to an external user can unintentionally reveal implementation details that are useful to an attacker for developing a subsequent exploit.

rules.cwe_name: Storage of File with Sensitive Data Under Web Root
rules.description: Exposing a node_modules folder, or the project folder to the public, can cause exposure of private information.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
rules.description: Building log entries from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of forged log entries by a malicious user.

rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Client-side URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.

rules.cwe_name: Assignment to Variable without Use
rules.description: If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Incorrect Block Delimitation
rules.description: The body of a control statement should have appropriate indentation to clarify which statements it controls and which ones it does not control.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If an HTML element has two attributes with the same name but different values, its behavior may be browser-dependent.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: A string transformer that does not replace or escape all occurrences of a meta-character may be ineffective.
